title: Analyzing perceptron algorithm for global gold price prediction using quantum computing approach
abstract_summary: The paper explores a Quantum Perceptron approach to predict monthly global gold prices using data from January 2018 to December 2022 and an 80:20 train–test split (training to Dec 2021, testing in 2022). The study provides an analytical demonstration of the quantum perceptron training and manual weight-update calculations, concluding that the method is feasible but requiring actual quantum hardware for full implementation and evaluation.
methodology_description: The authors performed an analytical study applying a Quantum Perceptron formulation to monthly global gold-price data. They obtained monthly gold prices (in Rupiah) from Kaggle covering January 2018–December 2022, split 80:20 (training: Jan 2018–Dec 2021, 48 months; testing: Jan–Dec 2022, 12 months). Each year was treated as a sample with 12 monthly variables: January–November as inputs and December as the target. Prices were converted to month-to-month percentage changes, then encoded into 2-bit binary symbols per month according to fixed percentage ranges (four classes mapped to two-bit codes), producing 24 input bits per sample (12 months × 2 bits). The model architecture used is a perceptron-style Quantum Neural Network with a 24-2-2 layout (24 inputs, 2 hidden units, 2 output units). Initial weights were set randomly (authors list an explicit set of initial weight vectors). The learning rule follows a quantum-perceptron update: compute hidden-layer net vectors Z via weighted sums, compute output vectors Y from Z, compare Y to binary target T, and update weights with W_new = W_old + alpha * (|Y> - |T>) * <X| (learning rate alpha = 0.1). The paper demonstrates a manual, step-by-step calculation for the first training epoch (computing Z1, Z2, Y1, Y2 and performing weight updates). Due to lack of access to a quantum device, training was not executed on quantum hardware or a simulator beyond these analytic/manual calculations; the procedure is presented as preparatory steps suitable for later execution on quantum computing resources.

results_summary: This paper presents an analytical exploration of a quantum perceptron algorithm for predicting global monthly gold prices. The authors describe dataset selection and preprocessing (percentage change → 2-bit encoding), define a 24-2-2 quantum perceptron architecture with randomly initialized 2-bit weight vectors and learning rate 0.1, and manually carry out the first training epoch including forward computation and explicit weight updates. No implementation on quantum hardware or full empirical evaluation (accuracy, MSE, runtime) was performed. The authors argue that quantum perceptron methods have potential advantages (efficiency, parallelism, faster convergence) but these remain untested in this study; they recommend further implementation and testing on quantum devices.
